BYLAW NO. 14767  
CITY OF BURNABY 
A BYLAW to amend  
Burnaby Taxation Exemption Bylaw 2023 
The Council of the City of Burnaby ENACTS as follows: 
This Bylaw may be cited as BURNABY TAXATION EXEMPTION BYLAW 2023, 
AMENDMENT BYLAW NO. 1, 2025. 
1.
Burnaby Taxation Exemption Bylaw 2023 is further amended by:
(a)
repealing section 1 in its entirety and replacing it with the following:
“Pursuant to section 224 of the Community Charter, Council does hereby 
exempt from taxation under s.197(1)(a) of the said Act for the 2026 taxation 
year, the lands and improvements, or portions of lands and improvements, set 
out in Schedule “A” to this Bylaw.”; and 
(b)
repealing Schedule “A” in its entirety and replacing it with Schedule “A” attached
to and forming part of this bylaw.
Read a first time this 14th day of October, 2025 
Read a second time this 14th day of October, 2025 
Read a third time this 14th day of October, 2025 
Reconsidered and adopted this 28th day of October, 2025 
MAYOR 
DEPUTY CORPORATE OFFICER

minutes_briefs.title: Burnaby renews property tax exemptions for non-profits for 2026
minutes_briefs.summary: Burnaby City Council has passed an amendment to its Taxation Exemption Bylaw, renewing property tax exemptions for the 2026 taxation year. This means that certain lands and buildings owned by the city or other public authorities and used by non-profit organizations—such as schools, community resource centres, and social service agencies—will not have to pay property taxes for that year. The bylaw lists the specific properties and the non-profits that benefit, including organizations like the Canadian Red Cross, Meals on Wheels, and the Burnaby Family Life Institute.
minutes_briefs.action_required: If you are a non-profit listed in the bylaw, no action is needed—your property tax exemption for 2026 is already approved.

key_dates.label: Burnaby 2026 property tax exemption takes effect
